purpose: Check runtime impact of composed workspace/controller extraction; no application behavior or scientific steps changed during this review.
method: One interpreter and dependency environment; separate baseline and candidate source paths.
Measurement workloads run sequentially, without tests/builds running alongside them.
Three fresh processes per version for workflows, navigation, sensor context and processing; order before/after, after/before, before/after. Each workflow has three inner repeats.
Summary uses the median of process medians; complete inner samples are retained. Frames within a drag and repeats within one process are not independent trials.
Nine fresh processes per version for each first-use graph probe; packaged pair zero is warmup and nine alternating pairs are retained.
OS and font caches are warm. Wall-clock measurements on shared Linux hardware have substantial variation; percentage differences alone do not establish a regression.
Correctness hashes, fixture creation and output verification are outside processing timers. Peak RSS includes those activities and excludes child processes.

Processing output digests use full JSON-normalized trees; non-finite values normalize to null. Loaded-frame hashes include dtypes, row/index values and attrs. Scientific-equivalence tests independently check schemas, labels and numeric values.
limits: Source and frozen Linux builds only; no Windows display, antivirus or cold-boot measurement.
Synthetic full-day TSDF data and synthetic graph tables; processing uses eight repetitions of a recorded IMU excerpt (97.4 minutes per recording), not independent day-long clinical recordings.
Peak process RSS is not the simultaneous total of parent and recording workers, nor a long-running memory-leak proof.
No claim of statistical equivalence from three independent timing batches.

profiling_followup.note: Separate instrumented runs, excluded from latency medians. Matching plot/render counts; observed accessor overhead is sub-millisecond across all nine actions.

prior_full_suite_same_candidate.note: Completed for candidate f9294cd before this performance review; application source is unchanged during the review.

validation.ordered_job_and_tab_routing: Two wiring differences covered by composition/order tests, included in focused test run

loading_separate_equal_frames.conditions: One process pinned to one allowed CPU; baseline imported as a separate package alias; same complete 8,640,000-sample TSDF and same interpreter/dependencies; one warmup pair then six alternating pairs; wall/CPU timers exclude hashing. No tests/builds alongside this control.

inspection_same_frame_object.conditions: Both function versions use the exact same DataFrame object, one process pinned to one CPU; full 8,640,000-sample TSDF; one warmup pair then four alternating pairs; no extra loaded frame is retained during inspection. Hashing outside timers.

graphs_same_process.conditions: Both baseline and candidate windows in one process, pinned to one allowed CPU, identical 6x30000 synthetic results; 30-minute view; one warmup pair then nine alternating pairs, three series checked per action. Includes queued Qt painting; GC instrumentation in both paths.

environment_setup_note: Initial candidate bundle layout rejected generated source egg-info shadowing installed dist-info through PYTHONPATH. Moved the ignored generated directory aside and rebuilt. Both final bundles use identical installed distribution metadata and pass layout/smoke checks; no application source fix was needed.

interpretation.startup: Small increase: packaged launch-to-report median 0.786 -> 0.815 seconds; in-app first-paint timer 0.432 -> 0.492 seconds. Different timing boundaries and noisy samples do not form an additive decomposition.
interpretation.ui: Independent-process graph-series and context-pan medians were sometimes higher. Same-process, same-CPU controls reduce the three-series difference to about 69 ms (1.197 -> 1.267 s); context panning varies in both directions. Graph and sensor-context pixels are identical, and plot/render call counts match. No large repeatable increase attributable to the extraction was established; small UI overhead is not ruled out.
interpretation.loading: Separate-process TSDF decode/statistic medians increased substantially even though all executing service files are byte-identical and no refactored UI module is imported by that benchmark. A separate-equal-frame control still varied; using the exact same DataFrame object gave 2.080 -> 2.157 s. This does not reproduce the 2.56x independent-process statistic difference. Do not present loading speed as conclusively unchanged or improved; repeat controlled Windows measurements before a performance guarantee.
interpretation.processing_and_storage: All complete normalized result digests match across versions and repeats; inputs and saved-run values are unchanged. Independent process timings vary, including opposite changes for single/two-recording processing. Their implementation files are unchanged.
interpretation.memory: Large sensor-context peak self RSS is about 623-624 MiB in both versions. No material peak growth in these workloads; this is not a long-running leak or total worker-family memory test.
existing_bottlenecks: Dense raw plots with three modalities take about 0.32-0.34 seconds per pan frame in these offscreen tests.
Saving a 66.6 MB / 600000-row JSON snapshot takes about 2.6-2.9 seconds at the independent-process medians; reopening about 2.2 seconds.
Selecting multiple detailed graph series still requires expensive Matplotlib rendering.
interpretation.follow_up: Repeat the provided benchmarks on the Windows packaged build and representative clinical files. Current evidence supports preserving scientific results, caching and UI layout, with small startup overhead and unresolved timing variance; it cannot prove zero performance impact on every platform.
